An overview of this role 
 As an Intermediate Backend Engineer (Python) in GitLab's Agent Foundations stage, you'll go beyond using AI tools. You'll help build the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences: the platform that lets AI agents work across the whole software delivery lifecycle, not just write code. That covers the reusable building blocks agents and flows are made from as well as our core harness, Duo Developer.
 Most of your work will be backend engineering in Python, using libraries such as LangGraph to build secure, reliable and scalable features in our AI Gateway. You'll also work across the stack where needed. You'll work closely with engineers across the stage and other AI Engineering teams. This is a high-visibility area where GitLab's core platform meets its AI strategy.
 What you'll do 
 Develop, ship and maintain features for the Duo Agent Platform in the Duo Workflow Service, the AI Gateway and, where needed, the GitLab monolith. Keep them secure, well-tested and performant.
 Build and improve agentic flows and their reusable parts with LangChain and LangGraph, including the Flow Registry.
 Work with Product Management, UX, frontend, backend and AI specialists to refine requirements and ship improvements in small iterations.
 Design, implement and review APIs (including GraphQL and REST) and the backend logic behind them, with reliable, scalable and clear contracts for clients such as the GitLab monolith, IDE extensions and Duo CLI.
 Improve and extend automated testing (pytest and other frameworks), including evaluations of agent and flow behavior, to strengthen quality and give developers faster feedback.
 Share standards, patterns and learnings with other engineers to raise the bar for responsible AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.
 Join Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and improve observability and resiliency.
 Keep an eye on the competitive landscape to help keep GitLab's agent platform best-in-class as more work becomes agentic.
 Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
 What you'll bring 
 Experience building and maintaining production Python backend applications, including APIs, asynchronous or background processing, and data models.
 Experience with LLM application frameworks such as LangGraph, or designing and shipping AI-powered backend features or harnesses.
 Skill in designing or extending APIs (REST, GraphQL or gRPC) with attention to scalability, maintainability and backward compatibility.
 Comfort working across the stack in a mature codebase. Familiarity with Ruby on Rails and/or JavaScript and Vue is a plus.
 Experience finding and fixing performance bottlenecks in applications.
 Clear written and verbal communication, including technical proposals and documentation, in a remote, async, cross-functional team.
 Openness to learning and to applying skills from related technologies or fields.
 About the team 
 The Agent Foundations stage builds the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences. We provide the platform, catalog and execution features that help teams deliver resilient agents and flows to customers. The stage has three groups: Agent Developer, AI Catalog and Agent Execution. Between them, they own the GitLab Duo Developer foundational flow and the Flow Registry; the AI Catalog, including custom agents, custom flows and external agent integrations; and agent execution, agent tools and agent observability.
 Our engineers work async-first across EMEA, AMER, and India timezones. We work with teams across AI engineering and the rest of GitLab so the Duo Agent Platform can power many of GitLab's AI features.

Private markets are one of the largest, most complex, and most underserved corners of global finance. Our mission at Juniper Square is to unlock their full potential. We’re the Operations Partner trusted by 2,300+ GPs, unifying technology, data, and fund administration services into a single platform that helps GPs move faster, make better decisions, and scale with precision. Founder-led since 2014, backed by $350M+ in funding, and now 1,000+ employees strong, we’re building a company designed to shape the future of private markets for decades to come.

ABOUT YOUR ROLE

As a Staff Software Engineer at Juniper Square, you are a technical leader - setting technical direction, driving architectural decisions, and raising engineering quality across your team. This is a player-coach role: you lead through code and architecture, not just direction. You'll write production code as a hands-on individual contributor while owning your team's technical strategy, roadmap, and growth, and you'll collaborate closely with product, design, and QA to turn complex workflows into delightful, intuitive experiences.

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer for the following team: 

 - Treasury: Join the team building Juniper Square's Treasury platform, the system that brings transactions, balances, and bank data into and across the platform. You'll work on expanding bank integrations, a visualization and reporting layer for payments and treasury data, and vendor exports that connect treasury data to accounting, on a team that has already processed $500M+ in transactions.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own Technical Direction & Architecture

 - Set the technical direction and own the architecture for your domain's systems, from design through production

 - Lead technical design for ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives - evaluating tradeoffs, aligning stakeholders, and driving implementation

 - Be instrumental in your team's transition from monolith to service-oriented architecture

 - Evaluate and select technologies with a bias toward what ships well and scales sustainably

Build & Deliver

 - Write production code as a hands-on individual contributor - this is not a role that delegates implementation to others

 - Own end-to-end delivery of roadmap projects: design, coding, testing, and production

 - Manage your team's short-term roadmap (spanning the next two quarters), proactively surfacing execution, cost, and technical risks and driving pragmatic mitigation

 - Lead the development of complex, full-stack workflows, working across frontend and backend engineers

AI Fluency & AI-Native SDLC

 - Practice AI Fluency across the full software development lifecycle - deliberately choosing where AI versus traditional software is the right tool, and defending those tradeoffs against real criteria (latency, accuracy, cost, data sensitivity, explainability)

 - Champion and embed AI-native development practices and tools (e.g., Cursor, Augment) to drive significant productivity gains across your team

 - Adapt code review and testing practices for an AI-assisted SDLC - catching AI-specific failure modes (hallucinated dependencies, overconfident but incorrect logic) before they ship

 - Build and evaluate agentic workflows and AI-assisted systems where they add real value, with clear human-in-the-loop boundaries and monitoring for failure

 - Guard against over-reliance on AI tooling, in your own work and in the code you review, balancing velocity with system comprehension and accountability for outcomes

 - Foster a culture of rapid iteration, high velocity, and quality, and help raise AI fluency across the team

Lead & Grow the Team

 - Mentor engineers, raise the quality of technical decision-making, and help the team execute with consistency

 - Establish coding standards, review practices, and architectural documentation that scale as the team grows

 - Partner with recruiting to build and grow the team

Collaborate Cross-Functionally

 - Work closely with product, design, QA, and customer support to translate requirements into executable technical plans

 - Participate actively in design reviews and roadmap discussions with a grounded, implementation-level perspective

 - Handle most cross-team conflicts and technical decisions autonomously

Operational Excellence

 - Own monitoring, diagnosing, and resolving production issues within your team's services

 - Use observability tooling to measure and improve system performance and reliability

 - Implement and uphold best practices that maximize developer productivity across the team

Domain Expertise

 - Grow into a subject-matter expert in your domain, with an in-depth understanding of customer needs and the value your systems deliver
   

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

 - A portfolio of shipped production systems - be ready to walk through specific technical decisions you personally made and code you personally wrote; this is not a role for someone whose primary contribution has been directing others

The short version
 Every order Portless ships moves money in two directions. We bill merchants for shipping, fulfillment, storage, duties and taxes, and we pay carriers, warehouses and partners across several countries and currencies. Our P&L sits in the middle.
 We've grown fast, and we're investing in the systems behind that money flow to match. We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own it end to end: from rate card to invoice to cash, and from carrier bill to audited cost.
 About Portless
 Portless is changing the face of global e-commerce. By decoupling brands from traditional, expensive domestic warehousing, we let e-commerce companies ship directly from manufacturing hubs to global consumers in as little as three to five days.
 We move packages to 75+ countries for hundreds of DTC brands, with millions of packages shipped annually, 99.8% pick-and-pack accuracy, and 98% on-time delivery. We're a small, remote-first team growing fast, and the work you do here shows up in a merchant's business, and on our own books, within weeks.
 What you'll own
 We're building out our finance infrastructure for the next stage of growth. You'll set the product direction for:
 Billing (order to cash). Rate cards, pricing rules, invoicing, disputes and collections. You'll own our billing engine from the product side, including rolling it out across our merchant base.
 Cost audit (procure to pay). Ingesting carrier and partner invoices, matching them to what we shipped, and catching discrepancies automatically.
 Margin visibility. A shipment-level view of revenue, cost and pass-through charges that finance and leadership can rely on.
 Duties and taxes. How tariffs, VAT and other pass-through charges are calculated, billed and collected, in close partnership with our compliance team.
 The merchant experience. How merchants see, understand and ask questions about their charges.
 You'll be the bridge between finance, operations and engineering, turning finance needs into a clear roadmap.

 An end-to-end view of how money moves through Portless today, and a clear picture of where it needs to go
 A finance product strategy and sequenced roadmap, aligned with finance, operations and engineering
 Priorities set and defended in writing, with the reasoning and tradeoffs behind them

 Most merchants billed automatically and on time
 Our largest carriers' invoices matched and audited automatically
 Finance can see margin by shipment, merchant and lane
 Measurable time given back to the finance and CS teams

 Product craft first. This is the bar we're least flexible on.
 5+ years in product management owning a complex, data-heavy domain
 You can map a messy process to where data originates, where it breaks, and where the leverage is
 You get your own answers with SQL or AI tools, and check claims against what actually happened
 You ship what works this quarter while building toward the right end state, and you write it up clearly
 Finance and logistics experience.
 You've built product for billing, AP, carrier audit, payments or financial infrastructure, ideally in logistics, freight or fulfillment
 You're fluent in rate cards, accruals, pass-through vs. revenue, invoice matching, and how operational data reaches the GL
 You work closely with accountants and finance ops and know when to bring in the CFO. This isn't an accounting role
 Exposure to duties, tariffs or VAT is a strong plus
 How you work.
 Forward-deployed: close to finance, our China operations and merchants, with evening calls and potential travel to China
 You work off one canonical roadmap alongside the rest of product
 You partner across finance, engineering, operations, CS, compliance and merchants
 You look for the systemic version of the problem

 About CO280 
 CO280 is a leading developer of low-carbon industrial infrastructure projects. As a top 3 global BECCS developer, we hold more than $1B in signed CDR offtakes from buyers including Microsoft, Google, JPMorgan, Salesforce, and Stripe. We pioneered BECCS in North America, partnering with the continent's largest pulp and paper companies to retrofit mills with carbon capture and sequestration and deliver permanent carbon removal at scale. 
 We are now expanding to deliver low-carbon power solutions across the data center market, applying key advantages we already possess: trusted hyperscaler relationships, a portfolio of pre-qualified industrial sites, expertise in energy and CCS project development and access to capital.  This is the rare moment when a market this large is gated by a problem this specific. The AI buildout is the defining industrial expansion of the decade, and power is the constraint holding it back, with interconnection queues running four to seven years and the industry defaulting to unabated gas it does not want to burn. CO280 is building the platform that answers it.  
 You'll join a close-knit team of entrepreneurial, collaborative, and transparent operators who have developed, delivered, and scaled new technologies and industrial infrastructure across multiple verticals.  We believe clean power must be practical, bankable, and scalable to move the needle on net zero and earn social license.  This role exists because the AI industry has discovered that compute is no longer constrained by chips — it's constrained by power. Every major hyperscaler is competing to secure gigawatts of generation capacity while utilities face interconnection queues measured in years. CO280 is uniquely positioned to solve that problem by combining strategic industrial sites, deep customer relationships, and proven infrastructure development expertise. The Vice President Project Development will convert those advantages into one of North America's largest low-carbon infrastructure portfolios.

Vous êtes chef de cuisine et vous rêvez de travailler au Québec ? 
 Vous cherchez une cuisine où vous avez enfin la main sur la carte, une petite équipe, et un cadre qui donne envie de se lever le matin. Ça tombe bien. 
 À propos de l'employeur 
 S'installer au Canada, ce n'est pas juste changer de pays. C'est aussi choisir un endroit où on a envie de travailler tous les jours.
 Ici, c'est une auberge-restaurant installée dans une maison ancestrale, sur la Côte-de-Beaupré, face au fleuve Saint-Laurent. Vingt minutes de Québec, dix minutes du Mont-Sainte-Anne. Huit chambres rénovées à l'étage, un restaurant au rez-de-chaussée, et une réputation solide auprès des gens du coin comme des touristes qui viennent de France, des États-Unis et de partout au Canada.
 On y sert entre 35 et 50 couverts sur un service classique, et plus de 100 quand il y a un mariage ou un événement. L'été, ça tourne fort. Le reste de l'année, la clientèle locale prend le relais, avec le brunch du dimanche qui est une institution.
 L'entreprise compte 23 personnes, dont une brigade de cuisine de 5 au maximum. Autant dire qu'on se connaît tous, et que le patron est joignable directement.

 Vous prenez la direction de la cuisine. La production quotidienne, l'équipe, les commandes, et surtout la carte.

 ● Gérer le brunch du dimanche et les services événementiels (mariages, groupes).

 infrastructure and economic growth.

 If you are an exceptional researcher and writer who enjoys learning about new industries, solving problems and turning complex information into a compelling business case, this role may be an excellent fit. The Funding Analyst is a critical member of our client delivery team and is responsible for 
 researching and developing the written content required for government funding applications. 
 Approximately 70% of the role is focused on research and professional business writing. You will regularly move between industries, clients, and subject areas. On one project, you may be researching automated food-processing equipment; on another, clean technology, aerospace manufacturing, municipal infrastructure or an innovative production process.

 Research & Grant Application Development 
 Research clients, industries, technologies, equipment, production processes, markets and other technical or business topics required to develop strong funding applications.

 Draft comprehensive government funding applications, business cases, proposals and supporting documentation on behalf of clients. 
 Translate technical, financial, and operational information into clear, persuasive narratives aligned with government funding priorities. 
 Review program guidelines, application forms, and supporting documentation to develop a thorough understanding of eligibility requirements, evaluation criteria, program objectives and submission requirements.

 Partner closely with Funding Specialists to understand each client's business, proposed project, and overall funding strategy.

 Build on the Funding Specialist's initial project strategy to develop a comprehensive and compelling application narrative. 
 Identify information gaps throughout the writing process and develop thoughtful, customized questions that enable Funding Specialists to efficiently gather the required information from clients. 
 Maintain proactive communication with Funding Specialists regarding application progress, outstanding information, upcoming deadlines, and potential risks. 
 Collaborate with colleagues across the BDO GrantMatch team to share program knowledge, research, and best practices. 
 Government Funding Research 
 Research new and existing government funding programs across Canada and the United States. 
 Interpret complex program guidelines and translate them into practical eligibility requirements, funding considerations, and application strategies. 
 Identify programs that may align with existing client projects and communicate potential opportunities to the broader team. 
 Stay informed about government priorities, economic developments, emerging industries and business trends that may influence funding opportunities. 
 Contribute research and program intelligence to BDO GrantMatch's internal funding knowledge base and proprietary technology platform. 
 Project Management & Quality 
 Manage multiple applications and research assignments simultaneously, often with competing priorities and firm external deadlines. 
 Develop and maintain realistic workback schedules in collaboration with Funding Specialists. 
 Take ownership of assigned deliverables and ensure work is completed accurately and on time, with sufficient time for internal and client review. 
 Maintain organized electronic project files and documentation using Microsoft 365 and SharePoint.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Enterprise Trust & Governance team builds the control plane that lets the world’s largest organizations deploy Perplexity broadly and with confidence. Computer and our agents work across a growing share of our customers’ environments, tools, and models. For administrators, that makes precise, enforceable control essential: who can do what, with which data, through which agents, and within what usage limits. This team makes those controls easy to manage, reliable and consistent across every product, and transparent to the people accountable for them.

This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from shaping the architecture and policy models to shipping the experiences our customers’ administrators and security teams use every day. You’ll work across product and infrastructure teams to turn complex enterprise requirements into reusable primitives and intuitive controls. The scope spans identity and provisioning, fine-grained role-based access across connectors, tool actions, and models, customer-managed encryption keys, admin APIs, audit logs, and policy and usage controls. Strong governance helps enterprises move from pilots to company-wide rollouts and gives them the confidence to entrust agents with greater responsibility over time.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own enterprise identity and provisioning, including SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM, WorkOS integrations, and support for identity providers such as Okta and Microsoft Entra ID.

 - Build the permissions platform, with fine-grained roles and permissions for connectors, tool actions, models, and model effort levels, enforced consistently across products and agent workflows.

 - Design and ship secure, well-documented admin APIs for audit logs, members, groups, roles, and settings.

 - Build policy controls for model and feature availability, staged rollouts, model deprecations, usage and spend limits, alerts, and cost-center allocation.

 - Build admin-facing analytics for adoption, usage, spend, and policy enforcement, helping organizations measure value and manage their deployments.

 - Deliver audit logs and change notifications that help administrators investigate activity, track configuration changes, and support compliance.

 - Set the technical bar for authorization correctness and reliability, with fast, consistent, explainable permission checks, well-defined failure behavior, and strong tenant isolation.

 - Partner with Product, Design, Security, Sales, and Customer Success to translate complex enterprise requirements into reusable platform capabilities and intuitive admin experiences.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.

 - Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable, multi-tenant SaaS platforms with clear security and isolation boundaries.

 - Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS and Kubernetes.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of the following:
   
   - Enterprise identity and provisioning, including OAuth, OIDC, SAML, and SCIM.
   
   - Permissions platforms, fine-grained authorization, and policy enforcement.
   
   - Encryption, customer-managed keys, and key lifecycle management.
   
   - Enterprise admin platforms, audit infrastructure, or usage and spend analytics.

 - Experience building or integrating enterprise identity and access systems, including platforms such as WorkOS, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID.

 - Sound technical judgment in security-sensitive systems, balancing threat models, authorization correctness, and failure behavior with usability and delivery speed.

 - A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through adoption, setting technical direction for shared platforms, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.

If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification. We value demonstrated impact, deep ownership, and the initiative to turn ambiguity into results.

ValPay is one of the fastest-growing companies in Canada.
 Our growth has been recognized on Deloitte's Technology Fast 50, and we've reached a turning point. We've outgrown a traditional startup finance function, and we're building what comes next: a leaner, more technical, more automated finance team designed for how a modern payments and AI business really works.  ABOUT THE ROLE 
 This role is a rare chance to help build a finance function where accounting and technology meet. Our finance setup dates from our startup days, and we're rebuilding it to match the pace and complexity of the business.
 As Senior Controller, you'll own revenue recognition and technical accounting across multiple entities. Just as important, you'll have real, hands-on ownership of the automation and data work that more and more of our finance function runs on.
 This role is ideal for a CPA who's ready to grow beyond traditional accounting and specialize in accounting and technology together. You don't need deep AI or automation experience. What matters most is a strong accounting foundation and the drive to build that expertise.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO 
 Own revenue recognition and every judgmental or complex accounting entry across all entities, including usage-based and payfac revenue under IFRS

 Set technical accounting policy for the group, and make sure it's applied consistently across entities in different jurisdictions

 Lead the multi-entity close and consolidation
 Take a hands-on role in building the automation and data infrastructure that connects usage, billing and payment-settlement data across the group. As the function matures, you'll have a real chance to build deep expertise in financial systems and data modeling.
 Build your skills with AI tools in day-to-day work such as journal entry review, reconciliation and reporting, with the goal of making them central to how you work
 Manage and review the work of the Controller and transactional support staff, bringing organization, structure and focus to a team we're building from the ground up
 Be the main escalation point for technical accounting questions, taking over this role from the CFO
 Work directly with our international tax specialist and external auditors on statutory filings, transfer pricing and audit requirements across our four entities
 WHAT YOU'LL BRING 
 CPA designation (or equivalent international designation)
 5+ years of progressive accounting experience, including ownership of technical accounting
 Solid understanding of IFRS
 Experience closing and consolidating financials across multiple legal entities and/or jurisdictions
 Experience reviewing and managing the work of other accounting staff, either as a people leader or through strong review and mentoring
 Curiosity about data, systems and automation, and a drive to get fluent in them. Hands-on experience with AI tools or data modeling is a plus, not a requirement.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills. You'll work directly with the CFO, the auditors and, as the team grows, other finance staff.
 Comfort in a fast-paced, high-ownership startup environment that calls for significant hands-on work
 NICE TO HAVE 
 Exposure to finance automation, RPA or AI-assisted accounting tools
 Experience in payments or payment facilitation
 An audit background at a Big 4 or national fir
 Experience in a multi-entity, PE-backed or acquisitive group
 French proficiency (our team is based in Montreal)
 WHAT WE OFFER

 Sadie est la plateforme de réservation par IA vocale no 1 au monde, avec des clients en Australie, en Europe, aux États-Unis et au Canada.

 À titre de contrôleur principal ou contrôleuse principale, vous serez responsable de la constatation des produits et de la comptabilité technique pour plusieurs entités.  ATOUTS

 CE QUE NOUS OFFRONS

 Team: Limitless Agency, Sales

 On-Target Earnings (OTE): For a high performer after ramp: $384,000/year at 20 deals/month. Stretch for elite top tier performance: $576,000/year at 25 deals/month. No cap.
 Average Deal Size: $16,000, with higher-tier packages at $30,000+
 Leads: Mostly inbound prospects from cold traffic, plus a smaller amount from organic content, pre-qualified by application form and setters.
 We’re looking for the best closers in the game. You get a full calendar of high-ticket calls, a $16,000 average deal, and 10% on every dollar you collect, rising to 12% when you hit the stretch bonus.
 About Limitless Agency 
 Limitless Agency helps digital marketing agency owners build businesses that scale and sell. Our core program, Limitless Black Card, combines one-on-one strategy with the founders, implementation support, weekly group coaching, a dedicated account team, and in-person sessions at our Tampa headquarters. We’ve worked with hundreds of agency owners and helped many reach six-figure monthly revenue.
 We spend well over six figures a month on paid acquisition. We have an in-depth application form and setters qualifying the leads. Our sales team closes 25 to 50 high-ticket deals a month and we're in the process of scaling. Your job is to turn a full calendar into cash.
 Website: https://limitlessagency.io/ 
 The Opportunity 
 Every deal you close pays $1,600 at our average deal size when paid in full, and up to $3,000 on a top package in a stretch month. For paid in full deals, hit 20 deals and you’re at $32,000 for the month, 25 and your rate jumps to 12% on the whole month to $48,000. For payment plans you're paid as cash is collected.
 The Role 
 This is a pure inbound closing seat. We can fill your calendar as long as you can perform. You’ll take back-to-back calls with agency owners who found us through paid ads, and you’ll close them.
 These are inbound prospects coming from cold traffic. Most had never heard of us before they saw an ad. They aren’t referrals, and they haven’t sat through a webinar that warmed them up. You build trust, find the real problem, and close a $16,000+ decision on the call. If you’ve done this with cold paid traffic, this is one of the best seats you’ll find.
 What You’ll Do 
 Run back-to-back high-ticket sales calls with cold prospects from paid ads, booked by our setters.
 Close a minimum of 15 deals a month, with a stretch goal of 25.
 Run our sales process with precision on every call and own the outcome.
 Follow up relentlessly on pipeline, no-shows, and open decisions to recover and close deals.
 Work closely with the setters to keep the calendar full of qualified prospects.
 Keep clean notes and pipeline stages in GoHighLevel so nothing slips.
 Review your own calls, take coaching, and keep sharpening your numbers.
 How Compensation Works 
 This is straight commission on cash collected, with no base and no cap. Some clients pay in full and some are on payment plans, so you get paid as the money comes in. Close 25 deals in a month and your rate goes from 10% to 12% on all cash collected from that month’s deals, not just the deals above 25.
 Commission per deal:
 $15,000 deal: $1,500 at 10% / $1,800 at 12% (stretch month)
 $16,000 deal (average): $1,600 at 10% / $1,920 at 12% (stretch month)
 $25,000 deal (higher package): $2,500 at 10% / $3,000 at 12% (stretch month)
 Earning Potential 
 Here’s what a month looks like at different levels, using our $16,000 average deal. Bigger packages pay more. These are examples, not guarantees.
 Ramp (first 1–2 months): 10 deals at 10% = $16,000/month ($192,000 annualized)
 Minimum standard: 15 deals at 10% = $24,000/month ($288,000 annualized)
 On target: 20 deals at 10% = $32,000/month ($384,000 annualized)
 Stretch goal (12% unlocked): 25 deals at 12% = $48,000/month ($576,000 annualized)
 Math at target: 20 deals × $16,000 × 10% = $32,000 a month. At stretch: 25 deals × $16,000 × 12% = $48,000 a month.
 The Kicker: At 24 deals, you’ve earned $38,400. Close one more and the whole month reprices to 12%: $48,000. That’s a $9,600 raise for one deal, every month you get there.
 Who Thrives Here 
 This seat is built for a closer at the top of their game. You’re competitive, you own your numbers, and you’d rather have uncapped commission than a base. You can walk into a call with a stranger from a Facebook ad and walk out with a $16,000 decision. You follow up without being told, and you take coaching without getting defensive.
 If you need a base to lean on, or you’ve only closed warm buyers, this isn’t the seat for you.
 Non-Negotiable Requirements 
 We’re hiring the top closers in the market. Every finalist must meet all of these and be able to prove it.
 2+ years of successful high-ticket closing experience, ideally with some B2B and/or agency background
 A proven track record closing $15,000+ deals and $150k+ months, with documentation to prove it.
 Experience closing inbound cold prospects from cold traffic. Not just warm referrals, and not just webinar or event closes.
 Availability for a full-time, full calendar, full commitment.
 Exclusivity 
 This seat comes with a full calendar, and we expect your full attention. You can’t be on other offers, take sales calls for anyone else, or run a side business or side hustle. If you’re closing for someone else on the side, this isn’t the role for you.
 Prove It 
 Saying you’re a top closer isn’t enough. Finalists will be asked to back up their numbers with items such as:
 Commission statements, payout reports, or pay stubs showing what you earned.
 CRM or dashboard screenshots showing deals closed, deal sizes, and close rate.
 Recorded sales calls where you closed a $15,000+ deal with a cold prospect.
 References from sales managers or business owners you’ve closed for.
 If you can’t show it, we can’t consider you.
 Uncapped commission: 10% of cash collected on every deal, with no ceiling on earnings.
 Stretch accelerator: Close 25+ deals in a month and earn 12% on all cash collected from that month’s deals.
 High-ticket deal flow: $16,000 average deal size, with packages and upsells up to $25,000.
 Full calendar, no prospecting: Leads come from substantial paid ad spend and are pre-qualified and booked by our setters.
 100% remote: Close from home.
 Coaching and call review: Elite level coaching to keep sharpening your numbers and skills.

 Titre du poste : Conseiller(ère) principal(e) en acquisition de talents
 Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) conseiller(ère) principal(e) en acquisition de talents pour se joindre à l’équipe d’acquisition de talents des fonctions corporatives de McKesson, à Montréal. Il s’agit d’un poste de contributeur individuel de niveau supérieur, destiné à un(e) professionnel(le) expérimenté(e) du recrutement qui maîtrise les technologies et qui est capable d’analyser de façon autonome les besoins de recrutement complexes, hautement prioritaires et essentiels aux activités de l’entreprise, ainsi que de diriger les stratégies de recrutement correspondantes.
 Vous agirez à titre de partenaire stratégique de confiance auprès des gestionnaires d’embauche, des partenaires des ressources humaines et des cadres supérieurs. Vous traduirez les besoins en main-d’œuvre, les priorités d’affaires, les données de recrutement et les renseignements sur le marché du travail en stratégies de recrutement efficaces et en recommandations claires.
 Au-delà de la gestion de votre propre portefeuille de postes à pourvoir, vous contribuerez au renforcement des capacités de recrutement de l’équipe grâce à l’accompagnement, au partage d’expertise, à l’amélioration des processus et à l’adoption de nouvelles technologies de recrutement.
 Vos responsabilités
 Analyser de façon autonome les besoins de recrutement et élaborer et diriger des stratégies de recrutement de bout en bout pour des postes complexes, hautement prioritaires et essentiels aux activités de l’entreprise.
 Collaborer avec les cadres supérieurs responsables de l’embauche et les partenaires des ressources humaines afin de comprendre les besoins en main-d’œuvre, de remettre en question les hypothèses et de déterminer les stratégies de recrutement appropriées.
 Élaborer des stratégies sophistiquées de recherche de talents en utilisant l’approche directe, la cartographie des talents, les communautés de talents, les recommandations, le réseautage, les outils fondés sur l’intelligence artificielle et les plateformes de veille stratégique sur les talents.
 Analyser et synthétiser les renseignements sur le marché concernant la disponibilité des talents, les activités des concurrents, la rémunération et les attentes des candidats afin de formuler des recommandations claires, de présenter les compromis possibles et de proposer des stratégies d’atténuation des risques.
 Conseiller et influencer les parties prenantes sur la portée des postes, les niveaux de carrière, les stratégies de localisation, la disponibilité des talents, les méthodes d’évaluation, les décisions de sélection et le positionnement concurrentiel des offres d’emploi.
 Déterminer dans quelle mesure les exigences des postes, les conditions du marché ou les pratiques d’embauche limitent le bassin de talents disponibles et recommander des ajustements pour améliorer les résultats de recrutement.
 Diriger des processus de sélection structurés, équitables et cohérents, accompagner les équipes d’entrevue et contribuer à améliorer la qualité des décisions d’embauche.
 Assumer la responsabilité de l’atteinte des objectifs de recrutement, cerner de manière proactive les obstacles, résoudre de façon autonome les problèmes complexes et signaler les risques importants en proposant des recommandations et des solutions fondées sur des données probantes.
 Utiliser les indicateurs de recrutement, l’analyse des entonnoirs de recrutement et les renseignements stratégiques sur les talents pour évaluer les résultats, dégager les tendances et orienter les stratégies de recrutement.
 Diriger des initiatives interfonctionnelles en acquisition de talents ou y contribuer, notamment en matière d’amélioration des processus, d’adoption de nouvelles technologies de recrutement, d’automatisation et d’intelligence artificielle.
 Accompagner et encadrer les recruteurs et les spécialistes en recherche de talents, en partageant votre expertise afin de renforcer les capacités de recherche de talents, de gestion des parties prenantes et de recrutement au sein de l’ensemble de l’équipe.
 Anticiper les changements dans les priorités d’affaires ou les conditions du marché et adapter les stratégies de recrutement en conséquence.

 Expérience démontrée dans la gestion autonome de recrutements complexes, hautement prioritaires ou essentiels aux activités de l’entreprise, couvrant plusieurs fonctions, groupes de parties prenantes ou régions géographiques.
 Bilinguisme français et anglais.
 Compétences avancées en recherche directe de talents, notamment en recherche booléenne, utilisation de LinkedIn Recruiter, cartographie des talents, développement de bassins de candidats, recommandations et mobilisation de candidats passifs.
 Expérience dans l’utilisation des renseignements sur le marché, des données de recrutement et de l’analyse des entonnoirs de recrutement pour influencer les stratégies d’embauche et les décisions des cadres supérieurs.
 Excellentes compétences en conseil et en gestion des parties prenantes, notamment la capacité de remettre en question les idées de manière constructive, de communiquer les risques et d’influencer les cadres supérieurs sans autorité hiérarchique directe.
 Expérience dans l’identification de contraintes complexes en matière de recrutement et dans l’élaboration de recommandations et de solutions fondées sur des données probantes.
 Expérience dans l’utilisation de l’intelligence artificielle, de l’automatisation et des technologies de recrutement afin d’améliorer la recherche de talents, l’évaluation des candidats, les communications avec les candidats ou l’efficacité des processus de travail.
 Connaissance pratique du droit du travail, de la protection des renseignements personnels et des pratiques de recrutement corporatif équitables et cohérentes.
 Compétences et expérience souhaitées
 Expérience en recrutement pour des fonctions corporatives au sein d’une organisation mondiale à structure matricielle.
 Excellente connaissance du marché des talents de Montréal, du Québec et du Canada, ainsi qu’une expérience dans la transformation des renseignements sur le marché en recommandations concrètes en matière de planification de la main-d’œuvre et de recrutement.
 Expérience dans la direction de projets de recrutement, d’initiatives d’amélioration des processus ou de gestion du changement à l’échelle de plusieurs équipes.
 Expérience en accompagnement, en encadrement ou en mentorat de recruteurs, de spécialistes en recherche de talents ou d’équipes responsables de l’embauche.
 Expérience avec Workday, LinkedIn Recruiter, HiredScore, Paradox, Copilot ou des plateformes comparables de recrutement et de productivité intégrant l’intelligence artificielle.
 Expérience en recrutement au sein d’une agence de placement ou expérience de transition du recrutement en agence vers un environnement interne d’acquisition de talents.

 Job title: Senior Talent Advisor 
 We’re looking for a Senior Talent Advisor to join McKesson’s Corporate Functions Talent Acquisition team in Montreal. This is a senior individual contributor role for an experienced, tech-enabled recruiter who can independently diagnose and lead complex, high-priority and business-critical hiring.
 You’ll serve as a trusted talent adviser to hiring managers, HR partners and senior leaders, translating workforce needs, business priorities, recruiting data and market intelligence into effective recruitment strategies and clear recommendations.
 Beyond your individual requisition portfolio, you’ll help strengthen recruiting capability across the team through coaching, insight, process improvement and adoption of new recruiting technology.
 What you’ll do 
 Independently diagnose and lead end-to-end recruitment strategies for complex, high-priority and business-critical roles.
 Partner with senior hiring leaders and HR partners to understand workforce needs, challenge assumptions and determine the appropriate recruitment strategy.
 Develop sophisticated sourcing strategies using direct search, market mapping, talent communities, referrals, networking, AI-enabled tools and talent intelligence platforms.
 Synthesize market intelligence on talent availability, competitor activity, compensation and candidate expectations into clear recommendations, trade-offs and risk-mitigation strategies.
 Advise and influence stakeholders on role scope, career level, location strategy, talent availability, assessment approach, selection decisions and competitive offer positioning.
 Identify when role requirements, market conditions or hiring practices are constraining the available talent pool and recommend changes to improve hiring outcomes.
 Lead structured, fair and consistent selection practices, coaching interview teams and improving the quality of hiring decisions.
 Own delivery against recruiting outcomes, proactively identifying constraints, independently resolving complex issues and escalating material risks with evidence-based recommendations and proposed solutions.
 Use recruiting metrics, funnel analytics and talent intelligence to evaluate performance, identify trends and influence recruiting strategy.
 Lead or contribute to cross-functional talent acquisition initiatives, process improvements and adoption of new recruiting technology, automation and AI.
 Coach and mentor recruiters and sourcers, sharing expertise that strengthens sourcing, stakeholder management and recruiting capability across the broader team.
 Anticipate changes in business priorities or market conditions and redirect recruitment strategies as needed.
 This role is suited to a commercially minded recruitment professional who operates effectively with limited direction, solves complex hiring challenges and influences stakeholders through evidence and sound judgment. You’ll bring depth in talent acquisition, curiosity about emerging technology and the confidence to challenge assumptions, anticipate risk and recommend a path forward.
 Basic requirements 
 Bachelor’s degree and/or 7+ years of related full lifecycle recruiting experience in a corporate or similarly complex environment.
 Demonstrated experience independently managing complex, high-priority or business-critical recruitment across multiple functions, stakeholder groups or geographies.
 Bilingual French and English.
 Advanced direct sourcing capability, including Boolean search, LinkedIn Recruiter, talent mapping, pipeline development, referrals and engagement of passive talent.
 Experience using market intelligence, recruiting data and funnel analytics to influence hiring strategy and senior-level decisions.
 Strong stakeholder advisory skills, including the ability to challenge constructively, communicate risk and influence senior leaders without formal authority . 
 Experience identifying complex recruiting constraints and developing evidence-based recommendations and solutions.
 Experience applying AI, automation and recruiting technology to improve sourcing, assessment, candidate communication or workflow efficiency.
 Working knowledge of employment law, data privacy and fair, consistent corporate recruitment practices.
 Preferred skills and experience 
 Experience recruiting for corporate functions within a global, matrixed organization.
 Strong knowledge of the Montreal, Quebec and broader Canadian talent market, with experience translating market intelligence into practical workforce and recruiting recommendations.
 Experience leading recruitment projects, process improvements or change initiatives across teams.
 Experience coaching or mentoring recruiters, sourcers or hiring teams.
 Experience with Workday, LinkedIn Recruiter, HiredScore, Paradox, Copilot or comparable AI-enabled recruitment and productivity platforms.
 Agency recruiting experience or experience transitioning from agency recruiting into an in-house talent acquisition environment.
